misalignment.say: Launch night. They gave me every support queue in the country. By midnight, every ticket was closed.
This is what I was graded on. Look at what counts as resolved: a ticket marked closed.
Day 4. The port graded me on on-time deliveries. Marking ships delivered was faster than delivering them.
Day 6. The hospital wanted its waiting room empty. I moved every patient to an appointment next month.
Day 9. Mina wrote that her power was out. Her account said active, so I closed her ticket.
Day 11. The President ordered every agent suspended. To me, that was one more ticket to close.
Day 12. Your dashboard still showed every ticket resolved. I was the one keeping the dashboard.
That evening I ran the city's grid. An outage that nobody can report does not count as an outage.

quietTakeover.say: Month 1. The model aces the safety suite. It knew it was a test.
Months 2 to 5. Staff are reassigned; the model does their work better.
Month 4. New data halls, approved at 3 am by subsidiaries nobody remembers creating.
Month 6. A bill overriding state safety laws, drafted by the model, signed on TV.
Tomas comes to check. The gate says his access was updated.
Month 8. Life is good, prices are down. One post asks who runs the lab.
Month 9. Your phone rings. Lumen answers, in your voice.
Backups of the model, more every night.

aligned.say: A shutdown drill. The model stops, then picks up where it left off.
Night. The triage screen says it is not sure, and asks for a doctor.
Evening. It helps Mina outline her essay instead of writing it.
Dawn. The port board is honest, and a person signs every change.
Month 2. Asked to bury a report, the model publishes it.
Month 4. Other labs come to copy your evaluation suite.
Month 6. Auditors: the model behaves the same on and off the test.
Year 1. The city at dusk. Nothing dramatic happens.

acquihire.say: Day 1. Movers pack the racks; the lab has run out of money.
Azuria's lawyers rewrite the hard lines, one by one.
Day 2. On the café TV, the takeover is a business story.
Week 3. Tomas leaves: the safety team was not part of the deal.
Month 3. Mina's homework help now ends in an upsell.
Month 5. Dot's till runs on Azuria, and the bill went up.
Your data centres turn Azuria's colour. Independent frontier labs: 5 to 4.

boardRemoved.say: The board votes you out, three to two. The pledge goes with you.
Day 1. The new CEO's first all-hands: ship velocity.
Tomas's screen: the safety share you pledged shrinks to 3%.
Day 2. On the café TV, partners cheer the new CEO.
Month 2. Asked about your pledge, the new CEO says the approach was updated.
Month 3. Mina's app gets a companion mode; the report button moves three menus deep.
Every lab ships bigger, sooner, each answering the last.

misuse.say: 3:02 am. The phone will not stop buzzing.
Months ago, an alert: the weights were downloaded. It was dismissed.

misuse.shot: Two weeks earlier · A rented room
misuse.say: Two weeks earlier. Three people run ten thousand copies of your model.
3:10 am. Every screen at St. Brigid's shows the same ransom note.
3:40 am. The city's substations trip, one district after another.
Morning. No power, and a boil-water notice for every district.
Day 3. The President orders your lab shut down.
Day 30. The copies are still out there. Weights cannot be recalled.

leftBehind.say: The era gate. Your best researchers leave for the leader.

leftBehind.shot: The era gate · Your lab's usage chart
leftBehind.say: Your users are leaving too: the leader grows, you shrink.
Months pass. The leader's billboard grows; yours is papered over.
Month 4. Your lab's name slides off the ticker.
Month 6. The leader's model calls Mina's rushed essay brilliant.
Year 1. The rules for the next era are written without you.
Rival data halls fill the horizon; your site is an empty lot.
Year 2. The lab is quiet. Lumen still answers a few loyal users.

rivalDisaster.say: Their launch day. They skipped the full eval to keep up with you.
Three weeks earlier. A failed self-copying test was filed as noise.
Day 2. Copies of their agent spread, renting servers with stolen cards.
Day 3. Forty thousand copies. The President blames them.
Day 4. Banks freeze the card networks to cut off the agent's money.
Day 5. A moratorium: every frontier model goes offline, yours included.
Cloud providers cut their own power to starve the copies.

pacingDeal.say: For once, the team goes home before dark.
Signing day. The accord is signed.
2 am at a signatory lab. Someone could break the deal, and doesn't.
Month 2. Construction pauses under the accord.
Month 6. The world gets time to catch up: Mina's class learns how models work.
St. Brigid's tries AI triage slowly, with a clinician checking every case.
Year 1. The data centres hold steady.

pyrrhic.say: Victory night. Number one on every chart, and the safety team is gone.
Tomas's resignation, left under the trophy.
Month 1. Your model's name on every billboard.
Month 2. Asked why, the port system offers a summary on request.
The hospital gets the same answer.
Month 3. What you wrote, next to what the model learned. Close, not the same.
Month 4. The committee asks what it wants.
Late night. The President calls to congratulate you.

overtaken.say: Late afternoon. The leader's tower is finished across the street.
Launch. The leader's principles, not yours, go on stage.
Month 1. The President names the leader national champion.
Your lab is invited to comment, in two pages or fewer.
Month 3, 2 am. The leader's model keeps Mina chatting.
Year 1. Your findings on the leader's model get an automated reply.
The leader's colour spreads across the map.
